title: Utility Order for Claiborne Electric Cooperative, Inc., ex parte. — Order No. U-37838 accepts the Uncontested Stipulated Settlement filed into the record on September 3, 2026, thereby authorizing CEC to extend its current FRP for one additional year, subject to certain conditions. The vote occurred at the Commission’s October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.

documents.text:
LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                  ORDER NUMBER U-37838

              CLAIBORNE ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE, INC., EX PARTE.

Docket No. U-37838, In re: Request for approval of one-year renewal of Formula Rate Plan.

               (Decided at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


                                            ORDER

  I.       Background

       On January 20, 2026, Claiborne Electric Cooperative, Inc. (“Applicant” or “CEC”) filed

its Application for One-Year Renewal of Formula Rate Plan, with supporting testimony and

exhibits (“Application”), with the Louisiana Public Service Commission (“LPSC” or the

“Commission”). Notice of the Application was published in the Commission’s Official Bulletin #

1368 on January 30, 2026, with a 15-day intervention period. There were no interventions in the

docket. In the Application, CEC requested an extension of its current Formula Rate Plan (“FRP”)

FRP for one additional year, the Test Year ending December 31, 2026. CEC did not request any

additional modification to the terms of its FRP.

 II.       Jurisdiction and Applicable Law

       The Commission exercises jurisdiction over common carriers and public utilities in

Louisiana pursuant to Article IV, Section 21(B) of the Louisiana Constitution, which states:

       “The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public utilities and have
       such other regulatory authority as provided by law. It shall adopt and enforce
       reasonable rules, regulations, and procedures necessary for the discharge of its
       duties, and shall have other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.”

III.       Staff Review and Uncontested Stipulated Settlement

       Commission Staff conducted a review of the Application and accompanying exhibits, as

well as CEC’s responses to formal and informal data requests. On June 30, 2026, Commission

Staff filed the Direct Testimony of Thomas Broady, with the Commission Staff Report and

Recommendation attached.

       Subsequently, CEC and Commission Staff reached an agreement with regard to the issues

in the docket, and executed an Uncontested Stipulated Settlement Term Sheet (“Uncontested

Stipulated Settlement”), which was filed on September 3, 2026. The Uncontested Stipulated

Settlement was presented at a stipulation hearing on September 18, 2026 pursuant to Rule 6 of the




                                                                             Order No. U-37838
                                                                                        Page 1
 Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure. The terms of the Uncontested Stipulated

Settlement are as follows:

1.         CEC shall be authorized a one-year (1-year) extension of its existing Formula Rate Plan
           (“FRP”) with a single test year ending December 31, 2026. CEC shall file its 2026 test year
           FRP annual report on or before March 1, 2027, with all the same prescribed terms and
           conditions of its existing FRP established by Order No. U-36552 dated February 19, 2024,
           and amended by Order No. U-36552-A dated April 26, 2024.
2.         Within thirty (30) days after the issuance of an order in this proceeding, CEC shall file into
           the record of this proceeding new or revised tariff pages reflecting the Commission’s action
           and shall submit a copy of the same to the Commission’s Utilities Division.
3.         No later than the expiration of this FRP’s extended term, CEC shall file with the
           Commission a full base rate case with a 2025 test year.


     IV.      Commission Consideration

           This matter was considered at the Commission’s October 22, 2026 Business and Executive

Session. On motion of Commissioner Campbell, seconded by Chairman Skrmetta, and

unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to approve the Uncontested Stipulated Settlement

filed into the record on September 3, 2026.

IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED THAT:

     1. The Uncontested Stipulated Settlement filed into the record on September 3, 2026 is
        accepted; and,

     2. This order is effective immediately.

BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
November 19, 2026
